/-!
# Erdős Problem 884

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
- [Tao25](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf)
- [Larsen](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf)
-/

namespace Erdos884

/--
The sum $\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i}$ over all pairs of
divisors $d_i < d_j$ of $n$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    ∑ j : Fin n.divisors.card, ∑ i : Fin  j,
    (1 : ℚ) / (Nat.nth (· ∣ n) j - Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i )

/--
The sum $\sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$ over consecutive
divisors of $n$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    ∑ i : Fin (n.divisors.card - 1),
    (1 : ℚ) / (Nat.nth (· ∣ n) (i + 1) - Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i)

/--
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty$, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i} \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an unconditional disproof.
-/
def Erdos884Prop : Prop :=
    sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference ≪ 1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference

/--
For a natural number n, let $1 = d_1 < \dotsc < d_{\tau(n)} = n$ denote the divisors of $n$
in increasing order.
Does it hold that
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \ll 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i}$
for $n \to \infty$, i.e.
$\sum_{1 \le i < j \le \tau(n)} \frac{1}{d_j - d_i} \in O \left( 1 + \sum_{1 \le i < \tau(n)}
 \frac{1}{d_{i + 1} - d_i} \right)$?

This conjecture has been **disproved**:
- In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer assuming the prime tuples
  conjecture, see `erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood` for this implication.
- Daniel Larsen subsequently gave an
  [unconditional disproof](https://github.com/Larsen-Daniel/Erdos-884/blob/main/884.pdf).

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/884](https://www.erdosproblems.com/884)
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/f8a51976fd2e66a52b4928c109fb9ae877a1a507/problems/884/Erdos884.lean"]
theorem erdos_884 :
    answer(False) ↔ Erdos884Prop := by
  sorry

/--
In September 2025, Terence Tao gave a conditional _negative_ answer to Erdos conjecture 884,
disproving it under the assumption of the *Qualitative Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture*.
See [here](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf).
The *qualitative* version of the conjecture only states that there are infinitely many tuples
of primes and does not require any asymptotical bounds and as such is a corollary of the general
form of the Hardy-Littlewood Conjecture.
We state the 'weaker' implication using general Hardy-Littlewood here, since this conjecture is
already formalized.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_884_false_of_hardy_littlewood :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m
    → ¬Erdos884Prop := by
  sorry

end Erdos884

findings.description: At lines 100–101, the quantifiers are outside the implication: `∀ k m, FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m → ¬Erdos884Prop`. This says that any single tuple's Hardy–Littlewood instance suffices, rather than assuming the conjecture for all tuples. With the current imported predicate, take `k = 0` and `m := fun _ : Fin 1 => 1`: the counting function is identically zero because `IsPrimeConstellation` requires `m 0 = 0`, so this hypothesis is trivially provable. In `/workspace/review/hypothesis.lean`, I proved, without using either problem theorem, that for arbitrary `Q`, `(∀ k m, FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m → Q) ↔ Q`. Thus the declaration expresses an unconditional conclusion in disguise, not the intended formulation of Tao's conditional result. Larsen's later unconditional disproof does not correct this quantifier-scope error.
findings.source_evidence: Tao, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf, p. 1: Conjecture 1.1 asserts infinitely many prime translations for every admissible integer tuple; Theorem 1.1 begins, “Assume Conjecture 1.1.” Section 2 takes an arbitrarily large K and applies the conjecture to a suitable K-tuple.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the universal quantifiers into the antecedent: `(∀ (k : ℕ) (m : Fin k.succ → ℕ), HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor m) → ¬Erdos884Prop`. This also requires correcting the imported predicate as described in the separate finding. Alternatively, assume the whole qualitative prime-tuples conjecture directly.

findings.description: The hypothesis does not mean the full Hardy–Littlewood conjecture advertised by the docstring. `HardyLittlewood.FirstHardyLittlewoodConjectureFor`, defined in `FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/HardyLittlewood.lean:61–66`, expands to `π_P =O[atTop] (fun n => C * ∫ t in 2..n, 1 / t.log ^ k.succ)`: only an upper bound, not an asymptotic formula. Such an upper bound supplies no prime-tuple existence; even an identically zero counting function satisfies it. This is independent of the quantifier-scope defect and remains after parenthesizing the universal hypothesis. Scratch checks confirm the distinction between big-O and asymptotic equivalence without using the repository's sorry theorems.
findings.source_evidence: Tao's Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.1, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/erdos-884.pdf, p. 1, require infinitely many prime translations of each admissible tuple. Tao adds that the full conjecture provides an asymptotic for their number. The imported module's cited source, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Hardy%E2%80%93Littlewood_conjecture, explicitly states `π_P(n) ∼ C_P ∫₂ⁿ dt/log^(k+1)(t)`, not merely an O-bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Tao's qualitative hypothesis directly: for every finite integer tuple h whose residues omit a class modulo every prime, infinitely many natural n have all n+h_i prime. A type-checked formulation is provided as `QualitativePrimeTuples` in `/workspace/review/hypothesis.lean`; assume that entire proposition before `→ ¬Erdos884Prop`. Alternatively, repair the imported quantitative predicate to use asymptotic equivalence (`Asymptotics.IsEquivalent`) for appropriately normalized, distinct admissible offsets, then universally quantify that corrected hypothesis.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses an eventual big-O bound as n tends to infinity, whereas the source asks for one absolute constant bounding the sums for every positive integer n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both divisor sums are nonnegative, and the comparison function `1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference n` is at least 1. A uniform bound therefore implies big-O. Conversely, an eventual big-O bound can be extended over the finitely many exceptional n by enlarging its constant. The extension to n=0 is harmless because both sums are zero there. I proved the exact equivalence with `∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → sumDivisorInvPairwiseDifference n ≤ C * (1 + sumDivisorInvConsecutiveDifference n)` in `/workspace/review/uniform.lean`, without using either problem theorem.

review.notes: All five declarations were checked. The main negative answer and research-solved tags agree with the source, which records DISPROVED (LEAN). The linked proof uses the same sum definitions and concludes the corresponding negated big-O statement; no sorry or custom axiom declarations were found, although its full external proof was not rebuilt. Lean checks established correct divisor enumeration, positive denominators for every actual summand, nonnegativity, and zero sums at n=0 and n=1. Proven-equivalent computable sums were evaluated for n=0 through 12. Arithmetic in the denominators is real subtraction, and the consecutive index is natural addition, not Fin wraparound. The passing scratch files are hypothesis.lean, sums.lean, and uniform.lean under /workspace/review; the substantive proofs have no sorryAx dependencies. The reviewed file remains identical to its committed version.

submission.summary: Corrected both reported issues by assuming the full qualitative Hardy–Littlewood conjecture: every finite admissible integer tuple has infinitely many natural-number translates consisting of primes. All tuple quantifiers now lie inside the antecedent, and the defective imported big-O predicate is no longer used. Updated the docstring and removed the unused import, leaving other declarations unchanged. The required compile command reports only the permitted `sorry` warnings.
